name: The Crevasse Fold

detectability.signature: Doubled starlight seam with lattice harmonics repeating at eleven-hour intervals out to 190,000 kilometers

proximity: Parallax doubles on every star near the seam
Range finders return contradictory readings within a light-second
Communications pick up ghost echoes of other lattice traffic
contact: Ship sections displaced by centimeters to meters across the fold
Cargo manifests cease matching their own holds
Translation along the lattice to destinations far beyond the seam
prolonged_exposure: Full translocation to distant nodes of the Builder network
Crew separated by folded meters, visible but unreachable
Vessels lingering at closure become permanently embedded in the lattice

phenomena: Stars doubled and offset around the seam
Ships exiting at locations far removed from their entry points
hazards: Dimensional displacement to unmapped lattice nodes
Equipment malfunction as calibration quietly lies near the seam
Separation of crew or cargo across folded space
opportunities: Access to regions of the Builder network otherwise unreachable
Hidden base location within sealed lattice pockets
Strategic chokepoint over one of the few working Precursor routes
known_incidents: 2298 - Liner Ciel d'Hiver arrived forty light-years off-course with all passengers unharmed
2317 - Keymaster Sarn Oduya vanished at seam closure; his keys did not
description: To the eye, the Crevasse Fold is a hairline seam of doubled starlight hanging in the dark, as if someone had sliced the sky and forgotten to heal it. Stars near the seam appear twice, offset by seconds of arc, and occasionally a strip of starfield simply shows the wrong season. The fold runs nearly forty-eight thousand kilometers end to end, a crevasse in space bridged by nothing.

The seam breathes on an eleven-hour cycle, gaping wide enough for careful hulls to slip between its faces before sealing to a hairline crack. Inside, distances lie: a hundred meters of transit has delivered ships to points light-years apart, always somewhere along the fold's ancient network. The Builders' lattice still routes traffic, but nobody alive reads its destination script.

Precursor archaeologists date the lattice's last rekeying to roughly two centuries ago, recent enough that some original intent survives. The liner Ciel d'Hiver emerged from a routine crossing inside a sealed tomb-system forty light-years off-course, her passengers unharmed and her itinerary ruined. Transit now requires a licensed keymaster who claims, truthfully so far, to feel the lattice's next breath coming.

The Compact Fold Authority maintains warning beacons along the seam and publishes cycle tables revised weekly and wrong monthly. Whoever built the crevasse intended something to pass through it forever, and the intention still works. Expeditions seeking the control stratum continue to depart, and continue to arrive somewhere else.
